'''Dan Margalit''' (born March 6, 1976) is an American [[mathematician]] at [[Vanderbilt University]]. His research fields include [[geometric group theory]] and [[low-dimensional topology]], with a particular focus on [[Mapping class group of a surface|mapping class groups of surfaces]].

==Education and career==
Margalit earned his bachelor's degree from [[Brown University]].<ref name="cv">{{cite web|url=https://people.math.gatech.edu/~dmargalit7/papers/cv_short_2019.pdf|title=Dan Margalit (Curriculum Vita)|date=2019|access-date=May 8, 2020}}</ref> He earned his doctorate from the [[University of Chicago]] in 2003, advised by [[Benson Farb]].  His thesis was titled ''Algebra versus Topology in Mapping Class Groups''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=75109 }}</ref> Margalit was a postdoctoral scholar at the [[University of Utah]] from 2003 to 2008.  He was a faculty member at [[Tufts University]] from 2008 to 2010, before going to the Georgia Institute of Technology.<ref name="cv" />  In 2023, Margalit moved to Vanderbilt University as chair of the Department of Mathematics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.vanderbilt.edu/news/2023/08/16/renowned-scholar-dan-margalit-joins-vanderbilt-university-as-professor-and-chair-of-department-of-mathematics/|title= Renowned scholar Dan Margalit joins Vanderbilt University as professor and chair of Department of Mathematics |last=Calhoun|first=Hollis|publisher=Vanderbilt University|date=August 16, 2023|access-date=September 12, 2023}}</ref>

Margalit is known for his work in exposition of geometric group theory, particularly his book with [[Benson Farb]], ''A Primer on Mapping Class Groups''.<ref name="primerreviews" />

==Awards and honors==
Margalit became a [[fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in 2019; he was recognized "for contributions to low-dimensional topology and geometric group theory, exposition, and mentoring."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=May 8, 2020}}</ref>  Margalit was a 2009 Sloan Research Fellow.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tuftsdaily.com/news/2009/03/12/math-professor-wins-research-fellowship/|title=Math professor wins research fellowship|work=Tufts Daily|date=March 12, 2009|access-date=May 9, 2020}}</ref>  For 2021 he received the [[Levi L. Conant Prize]] of the AMS.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/pabrowse.cgi?parent_id=29 Levi L. Conant Prize 2021]</ref> For 2024 he was awarded the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Mathematical Exposition.<ref>[http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7251 Leroy P. Steele Prize 2024]</ref>
